records.title: Tough constructions
records.objective: Use patterns such as This problem is difficult to solve with correct understood object relations.

concept.en: In a tough construction, the matrix subject is understood as a missing object inside the infinitive clause: This problem is difficult to solve.
concept.vi: Trong tough construction, chủ ngữ mệnh đề chính được hiểu là tân ngữ bị khuyết bên trong infinitive: This problem is difficult to solve.

formulae: NP + be + easy/difficult/impossible + to-infinitive with object gap
whenToUse: Use the construction only when the matrix subject can be interpreted as the semantic object or complement of the infinitive.

positive: The final paragraph is difficult to interpret without the earlier definition.
This valve is awkward to reach when the outer panel is fitted.
The distinction is easy to overlook in a rapidly edited document.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled C2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Supplementive participial clauses
records.objective: Use detached non-finite clauses to add circumstance/comment without dangling reference.

concept.en: Supplementive non-finite clauses are loosely attached comments or circumstances whose understood subject must be recoverable from the host clause.
concept.vi: Mệnh đề không chia supplementive là phần bình luận/hoàn cảnh gắn lỏng, với chủ ngữ ngầm phải suy ra rõ từ mệnh đề chính.

whenToUse: Use supplementives to add secondary circumstance or evaluation without creating dangling reference.

positive: Concerned about the widening confidence interval, the analysts ran a second robustness check.
The committee rejected the proposal, citing unresolved questions about enforcement.
Still uncertain about the source of the leak, engineers kept the affected line isolated.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled C2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Absolute clauses
records.objective: Use noun + participle/adjective/preposition supplements independently of main-clause subject.

concept.en: Absolute clauses contain their own explicit subject plus a non-finite, adjective, or prepositional predicate and modify the whole main clause.
concept.vi: Absolute clause có chủ ngữ riêng cùng vị ngữ không chia, tính từ hoặc giới từ và bổ nghĩa cho toàn mệnh đề chính.

formulae: noun phrase + participle/adjective/prepositional phrase, main clause
whenToUse: Use absolutes for compact background circumstances when their relation to the main event is clear.

positive: The final vote having been postponed, both delegations agreed to continue informal talks.
All other factors equal, the revised method produces a slightly lower estimate.
Her hands in her pockets, the witness waited silently outside the hearing room.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled C2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Verbless clauses
records.objective: Use compact subordinate/supplement clauses such as when necessary/though difficult appropriately.

concept.en: Verbless clauses omit an understood form of be and often function as compact conditional, concessive, temporal, or supplementive clauses.
concept.vi: Verbless clause lược dạng be có thể suy ra và thường làm mệnh đề điều kiện, nhượng bộ, thời gian hoặc supplementive cô đọng.

whenToUse: Use verbless clauses when the omitted copula and subject relation are unmistakable; restore a finite clause if ambiguity arises.

positive: When necessary, the regulator may require an independent valuation.
Though technically feasible, the proposed migration would be prohibitively expensive.
Once fully operational, the new facility should process twice the current volume.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled C2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Prepositional phrase attachment and ambiguity
records.objective: Detect and rewrite structures where a prepositional phrase has multiple plausible attachments.

concept.en: A prepositional phrase may plausibly modify a verb, noun, or another phrase; attachment ambiguity can change who did what or with what.
concept.vi: Một cụm giới từ có thể bổ nghĩa hợp lý cho động từ, danh từ hoặc cụm khác; mơ hồ attachment có thể làm đổi ai làm gì hoặc bằng công cụ nào.

formulae: verb + NP + PP with multiple attachment sites
whenToUse: Detect competing parses and rewrite by repositioning, adding a relative clause, or naming the intended relation explicitly.

positive: Using the new scanner, the analyst examined the document that had been stored in the archive.
We discussed the proposal from the regional office during the afternoon session.
The team photographed the device with the cracked housing, not with a telephoto lens.

records.title: Articles with proper names and institutional titles
records.objective: Handle marked article use with newspapers, organizations, families, landmarks and renamed entities.

concept.en: Proper names are usually articleless, but conventional classes such as newspapers, families, plural states, organizations, seas, and descriptive landmarks take marked article patterns.
concept.vi: Tên riêng thường không có mạo từ, nhưng các nhóm quy ước như báo chí, gia đình, quốc gia số nhiều, tổ chức, biển và địa danh mô tả có mẫu mạo từ riêng.

formulae: the + selected organizations/newspapers/plural or descriptive names
whenToUse: Treat article choice with proper names as a conventional naming property and distinguish official titles from generic descriptions.

positive: The Netherlands submitted its revised position to the United Nations before the deadline.
She cited an editorial published in The Guardian during the earlier debate.
Mount Etna was visible from the coast, while the Mediterranean remained unusually calm.

records.title: Countability shifts and coercion
records.objective: Use mass nouns as countable instances/types and count nouns as substances/activities when context licenses it.

concept.en: Context can coerce a normally mass noun into a count reading for types, portions, or instances, or a count noun into a mass-like reading for substance/activity.
concept.vi: Ngữ cảnh có thể ép danh từ thường không đếm được sang cách đọc đếm được cho loại/phần/trường hợp, hoặc ngược lại cho vật chất/hoạt động.

formulae: count noun → mass/substance reading where context licenses
whenToUse: Use coerced countability only when the contextual interpretation is natural and recoverable.

positive: The tasting compared three coffees grown at different altitudes.
The committee encountered two distinct resistances to the reform: legal and cultural.
There was chicken on the floor after the container split open.
